c.tagline: Vietnam's largest island, ringed by white-sand beaches, fish-sauce villages, and the world's longest sea cable car

card: Widely accepted at resorts; cash preferred at markets and small local eateries

taxi.fareNote: Grab is widely used and reliable across the island

emergency.note: 113 for police, 115 for medical emergencies; resort areas have some English support

walk: Duong Dong town is walkable for its market and waterfront; the island's beaches and attractions are spread out and best reached by scooter, taxi, or Grab

safety.safety: Very safe island, popular with families and honeymooners
safety.crime: Petty theft on crowded beaches is the main concern

hood_landmark.Duong Dong (Town Center): Duong Dong Night Market and Dinh Cau Rock Temple
hood_landmark.An Thoi (South): An Thoi's harbor and cable car terminal
hood_landmark.Bai Sao (Sao Beach): Bai Sao's white sand and turquoise shallows

avoid.reason: Inspect and photograph rental motorbikes to avoid damage scams, watch bags at the night market, and take care on unlit roads after dark.

hood_desc: The island's main town, with the night market, fishing harbor, and most everyday services; a lively, less resort-y base.
The island's famous sunset-facing beach strip, lined with resorts, beach clubs, and restaurants.
The southern port town and departure point for the Hon Thom cable car and boat trips to the An Thoi archipelago.
One of the island's most photographed beaches, with powder-white sand and shallow turquoise water.
A quieter, less developed northern area with forest, small beaches, and views toward Cambodia.

JW Marriott Phu Quoc Emerald Bay
Blue Hotel Sunset Town Phu Quoc

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only.

transit.sys: Grab and local taxis; scooter rental is very popular
transit.map: Not centrally published; scooter rental is the most flexible way to explore
transit.note: Renting a scooter is common for visitors comfortable riding; otherwise Grab covers the island well

transport.air: Phu Quoc International Airport (PQC), with direct domestic and some international flights
transport.bus: Local buses connect the airport, Duong Dong, and Long Beach
transport.ferry: High-speed ferries connect to Ha Tien and Rach Gia on the Vietnamese mainland
transport.car: Rental cars and scooters are available; roads circle most of the island

net.m: Good 4G coverage across most of the island
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Viettel or Vinaphone tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory but appreciated for tour guides

landmarks: Sao Beach (Bai Sao)
Powder-white sand and swaying palms curve around jade shallows on the island's southeast coast, making this Phu Quoc's most photographed stretch of beach.
Hon Thom Cable Car
Gliding nearly eight kilometers over turquoise sea and fishing fleets to Pineapple Island, this is the world's longest three-wire oversea cable car ride.
Long Beach (Bai Truong)
Twenty kilometers of golden sand fringe the island's west coast, where beach bars serve cocktails to some of Vietnam's most reliable and romantic sunsets.
Dinh Cau Rock (Cau Temple)
A tiny 17th-century temple-lighthouse perched on wave-sculpted rocks guards Duong Dong's harbor, where fishermen still pray for safe passage before sailing.
Phu Quoc Prison (Coconut Tree Prison)
This sobering wartime prison museum preserves cells, barbed wire and stark dioramas documenting the harsh treatment of prisoners during the Vietnam War.
Duong Dong Night Market
Grilled sea urchins, peppercorn crab and coconut ice cream draw evening crowds to this buzzing gauntlet of seafood stalls and souvenir vendors.
Phu Quoc National Park
Covering more than half the island, this UNESCO-recognized biosphere of primary rainforest hides trekking trails, rare wildlife and streams beneath dense canopy.
Ho Quoc Pagoda (Truc Lam Zen Monastery)
The island's largest Buddhist temple complex cascades down a forested hillside, its dragon-flanked staircases framing sweeping views over the East Sea.
Suoi Tranh Waterfall
A gentle jungle stream tumbles through mossy boulders and rock pools, offering a shady rainy-season swim just outside Duong Dong town.
Ham Ninh Fishing Village
Stilt houses and a long wooden pier stretch into shallow jade water, where villagers sell just-caught flower crab beneath the Ham Ninh mountains.

train.note: Phú Quốc is an island in the Gulf of Thailand with no railway of any kind, and Vietnam's rail network does not reach the Mekong Delta at all - the southern terminus of the Reunification Line is Ho Chi Minh City's Saigon station (Vietnam Railways, https://dsvn.vn/). To combine rail with the island you would take a train to Saigon and then a bus to Rạch Giá or Hà Tiên for the ferry, or simply fly. There are consequently no international trains either.

bus.note: There is no bridge or road causeway to Phú Quốc, so buses only get you as far as the mainland ferry ports: FUTA Bus Lines (Phương Trang, https://futabus.vn/) runs frequent coaches from Ho Chi Minh City to Rạch Giá (about 6-7 hours) and Hà Tiên (about 8 hours), often sold as a through bus-plus-boat ticket. Once on the island, minibuses and taxis meet each sailing at Bãi Vòng and An Thới ports, with shared minibus seats sold on board. Cambodia is close by across the water but there is no scheduled cross-border bus or boat, so travellers from Sihanoukville or Kampot go overland to Hà Tiên and take the ferry.

intl.to: Rạch Giá (Vietnam) - high-speed catamaran, about 2.5 hours to Bãi Vòng port
Hà Tiên (Vietnam) - high-speed catamaran, about 1.5 hours; slower car ferry about 2.5 hours
Rạch Giá & Hà Tiên (Vietnam) - fast ferries and car ferries

ferry.note: Superdong and Phu Quoc Express both run the two mainland routes: Hà Tiên is the shortest crossing at around 90 minutes, while Rạch Giá takes about 2.5 hours but connects better with buses from Ho Chi Minh City. Fast boats dock at Bãi Vòng on the island's east coast, roughly 25 km from Dương Đông, while the roll-on car ferries use Đá Chồng and An Thới, so check which port your ticket names before arranging a pick-up. Cars and motorbikes must be booked ahead, especially at Tết and in the July-August domestic holiday peak, and sailings are regularly cancelled in rough weather between roughly October and December.

half.name: Hon Mong Tay
half.blurb: Small islet in the An Thoi Archipelago, reached by boat in under an hour, is a common snorkeling stop known locally as Fingernail Island.

half.name: Hon Roi
half.blurb: Rocky islet south of Phu Quoc, part of the An Thoi boat-tour circuit, offers coral reef snorkeling in shallow, clear water.

half.name: Turtle Island
half.blurb: Small uninhabited island in the An Thoi group, visited on the same boat circuit as nearby islets, has a narrow sand beach used for lunch stops.
